title: WPPIL/49/2018 of In Re In The Matter Of Suo Motu Congnizance Regarding Contamination Of Water Of River Ganga Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (PIL) No. 49 of 2018
In Re,
"In the matter of Suo Moto Coginzance Regarding
Contamination of Water of River Ganga
 .........Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others. ........Respondents
Mr. D. Barthwal, Amicus Curiae, for the petitioner.
Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, Standing Counsel for the Government of India.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Chief Standing Counsel with Mr. B.S.
Parihar, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate for the Peyjal Nigam.
Coram: Hon'ble Rajiv Sharma, ACJ.
 Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Dated: 04th October, 2018
Rajiv Sharma, ACJ (Oral)
 In sequel to the previous orders passed by this
Court, counter affidavit has been filed by Secretary,
Drinking Water to the State of Uttarakhand.
2. The River Ganga originates from the State of
Uttarakhand. Number of small towns, cities, Nagar
Nigam, Nagar Panchayat and villages are situate on the
banks of River Ganga and its Tributaries. Hundreds of
drains discharge directly into River Ganga and its
tributaries without treatment. It pollutes River Ganga.
The drains discharging untreated water into River Ganga
and its tributaries are required to be tapped. It is in this
background that the directions were issued on the
previous date to the State of Uttarakhand to file affidavit.
3. According to the averments made in Paragraph
No.4 of the counter affidavit, out of 135 drains, 70 drains
were tapped in earlier programs namely Ganga Action
Plan (GAP) Phase-I, GAP Phase-II, National Ganga River

2
Basin Authority (NGRBA). Out of remaining 65 untapped
drains, Interception, Diversion and Treatment (I&D and
STP) of 59 drains were approved by the National Mission
for Clean Ganga (hereinafter referred to as NMCG) in
March, 2017 under Namami Gange Program through 18
DPRs. These (I&D and STP) are in various stages of
execution. The averments made in Paragraph No.4 are
vague and sketchy. There is no separate time schedule
given for tapping of 59 drains.
4. Now, as far as remaining 06 untapped drains
are concerned, the remedial measures are being
undertaken under the guidance of NMCG.
Direction: There shall be a direction to the State
Government and the Executing Agencies including the
Contractors to seal and divert 65 untapped drains which
discharge water without treatment into River Ganga or its
tributaries forthwith.
5. According to the averments made in the
affidavit, 60 number of cleaning staff of Nagar Nigam and
an outsourcing agency has been engaged for regular
drain cleaning works along with use of four vehicles on
regular basis. 30 iron screens/jallies have been fixed at
various places to check the floating waste. The Ghat
cleaning project for 72 Ghats of Haridwar has already
been sanctioned by NMCG for three years vide letter
dated 17.07.2018. The Implementing Agency for the
project is Nagar Nigam, Haridwar. 400 cleaning staff
along with modern cleaning equipments will be deployed
for regular cleaning works. Tender process for these
projects is scheduled to be published by 30th September,
2018.

3
Direction: There shall be a direction to the Nagar Nigam,
Haridwar to complete the tender process within twenty-one days from today and thereafter, to issue the work
orders for cleaning of 72 Ghats of Haridwar.
6. The Trash Skimmer has been deployed by
NMCG at Haridwar to collect all kinds of floating waste
on river surface. The collected waste is being regularly
transported to the identified disposal point from where
the Urban Local Body is entrusted to do scientific
disposal. The DPR has been submitted by Urban
Development Department costing Rs.118.19 lakhs
regarding installation of additional M.S. Angle Iron Mesh
and deployment of additional manpower for regular
cleaning of various drains in Haridwar, Rishikesh and
Muni-ki-Reti. It has been forwarded to NMCG for
appraisal and budgetary support under the Namami
Gange Programme vide letter dated 08.08.2018.
Direction: The NMCG is requested to accord the
necessary sanction for the aforesaid tasks within a period
two months from today.
7. Now, we will advert to the ground realities in
Rishikesh. Four drains i.e. PWD Drain, Saraswati Drain,
Bengali Basti Drain, Swargashram Drain have been
tapped. Sai Ghat Drain and Sant Seva Ashram Drain are
untapped. For tapping and permanent treatment of these
drains, execution of theI&D/STP works are ongoing
which is scheduled to be completed by November, 2019.
Direction: There shall be a direction to the State
Government and the Executing Agencies including the
Contractors to ensure that the work is completed on or
before June, 2019, since two drains are emptying into

4
River Ganga. There shall also be direction to the
respondents to ensure that no untreated water flows
from untapped trains i.e. Sai Ghat Drain and Sant Seva
Ashram Drain into River Ganga. In other words, these
drains are ordered to be sealed and diverted forthwith.
8. In Muni-ki-Reti, six drains are untapped. The
tapping and permanent treatment of these drains,
execution of I&D/STP works are ongoing which is
scheduled to be completed by August, 2019. However,
taking into consideration the emergent situation, these
drains cannot be permitted to drain out into River Ganga
without treatment. These drains are ordered to be sealed
and diverted forthwith.
9. In Tapovan, all five drains are tapped.
10. In Devprayag, all drains are tapped.
11. In Kirti Nagar, two drains are untapped. The
execution of I&D/STP works are completed and are
under trial and testing. These drains are ordered to be
sealed and diverted forthwith. The work already
undertaken is ordered to be expedited and trial and
testing be completed within a period of one month from
today.
12. Now, we will advert to Srinagar. Seven drains
are tapped. Ten drains are untapped. It is an alarming
situation. The fact that these ten drains are untapped is
suggestive of the factum that the untreated water is
drained out along with effluents directly into River Ganga
or its tributaries. The tapping and permanent treatment
of these drains is going on and it is scheduled to be
completed by January, 2019.

5
Direction: There shall be direction to the State
Government and the Executing Agencies including the
Contractors to ensure that the tapping work is completed
on or before 01.02.2019.
13. In Srikot- Gangnali, there are five untapped
drains. The DPR of 5 drains was earlier sent to NMCG for
approval. Certain observations were made by NMCG. 01
Drain as has been identified for In-situ remediation. As
soon as the list of Approved Technologies and Vendors
regarding In-Situ treatment is approved and shared by
NMCG, the DPRs of 02 Drains will be submitted to
NMCG/ GoI for approval.
Direction: The process be expedited and all codal
formalities be completed within three months from today.
14. Rudraprayag has a very grim situation. All
eight drains drain out directly into River Ganga without
treatment. None of these drains have been tapped. The
work is going on and an assurance has been made that
the same will be completed on or before February, 2019.
Direction: Till the work is completed, these drains are
ordered to be sealed and diverted forthwith. There shall
also be a direction to the State Government and the
Executing Agencies including the Contractors to complete
the work on or before 01.03.2019.
15. In Karnprayag, the situation is not different.
There are seven drains which are untapped. The work, as
per the affidavit, would be completed by November, 2018.
Direction: Till the work is completed, these drains are
ordered to be sealed and diverted forthwith. There shall
also be a direction to the State Government and the

6
Executing Agencies including the Contractors to complete
the work on or before 01.12.2018.
16. In Nandprayag also there are three drains
which are untapped. The assurance has been given that
the work would be completed by October, 2018, as per
the Contract Agreement.
Direction: There shall be a direction to the State
Government and the Executing Agencies including the
Contractors to complete the work on or before
01.11.2018. Till then, these drains are ordered to be
sealed and diverted forthwith.
17. In Gopeshwar-Chamoli, there are seven drains
which are untapped. The assurance has been given that
the work would be completed by February, 2019.
Direction: There shall also be a direction to the State
Government and the Executing Agencies including the
Contractors to complete the work on or before
01.03.2019. Till then, these drains are ordered to be
sealed and diverted forthwith.
18. In Joshimath also, there are five drains which
are untapped. The assurance has been given that the
work would be completed by April, 2019.
Direction: There shall also be a direction to the State
Government and the Executing Agencies including the
Contractors to complete the work on or before
01.05.2019. Till then, these drains are ordered to be
sealed and diverted forthwith.
19. In Badrinath, there are six drains, out of
which, two are tapped and four are untapped. For
tapping and permanent treatment of these drains,

7
executions of the I&D/STP works are ongoing. Works are
scheduled to be completed by May-2019.
Direction: There shall be a direction to the State
Government and the Executing Agencies including the
Contractors to complete the work on or before
01.06.2019. Till then, these drains are ordered to be
sealed and diverted forthwith.
20. In Uttarkashi, there are four drains. All of
them have been tapped. We place our appreciation for
the work undertaken by the State Agencies to tap these
four drains at Uttarkashi.
21. A startling revelation has also been made in
Paragraph No.9 of the short counter affidavit, filed by the
State Government. According to the averments made in
Paragraph No.9, the sewage/waste generation of the 15
priority towns (present general and projected generation)
in another 10 years comes to 187.57 MLD against which,
61.89 MLD capacity treatment facility presently exists
and additional 126.05 MLD treatment capacity is
required. Uttarakhand Peyjal Nigam has prepared 18
DPRs, which include 13 projects for interception and
diversion (I&D) of 59 drains, as well as installation of 31
new STPs of 131.75 MLD treatment capacity in 11 towns
namely Haridwar, Rishikesh, Muni-ki-Reti, Dhalwala,
Kirti Nagar, Srinagar, Rudraprayag, Karnprayag,
Nandprayag, Gopeshwar, Joshimath, Badrinath. There
are also five projects for upgradation of Six existing
Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) in five towns namely,
Haridwar (2 STPs), Tapovan, Swargashram, Gyansu and
Srinagar. These DPRs were appraised by the Indian
Institute of Technolgy, Roorkee. After appraisal by IIT,
Roorkee, NMCG sanctioned the said 18 DPRs amounting

8
to Rs.885.20 crore in the year 2017 for the construction
of 31 new STPs with existing STPs in five towns and also
I&D of 59 untapped drains in 11 towns as per the local
need. All 18 DPRs/projects pertaining to identified
priority towns were sanctioned by NMCG from time to
time in the year 2017. The present status as on
30.08.2018 and the schedule of completion of these 18
projects is given in a tabular form as under:-

22. The upgradation of Tapovan STP is complete
and is under trial along with Kirti Nagar, I&D of drain
with STP.
Direction: The trials of STPs be completed and the
Sewage Treatment Plants be made functional within a
period of three months from today.
23. The projects of Nandprayag, I&D with STP,
Karnprayag, I&D with STP, upgradation Gyansu STP,
upgradation Swargashram STP and Arihant Vihar
Haridwar, Sewer Networking have been completed only
upto 51.27%, 36.87%, 71.37%, 87% and 49%
respectively.
Direction: Accordingly, there shall be a direction to the
State Government and the Executing Agencies including
the Contractors to complete the work and to make the
Sewage Treatment Plants functional in Nandprayag, I&D
with STP, Karnprayag, I&D with STP, upgradation
Gyansu STP, upgradation Swargashram STP and Arihant
Vihar Haridwar, within a period of six months from
today.
24. Five projects shall be completed by the end of
March, 2019 including Gopeshwar I&D with STP,
Rudraprayag I&D with STP, Srinagar I&D with STP,
Upgradation Srinagar STP and Upgradation Haridwar
STPs. The percentage of work executed till 30.08.2018
shows a grim picture. The progress of only 32%, 31%,
31.9%, 20%, 20.88% in 27 MLD and 20.07% in 18 MLD
STP has been made in the aforesaid five projects.

10
25. Taking into consideration the present status,
as on 30.08.2018, there shall be a direction to the State
Government and the Executing Agencies including the
Contractors to complete the projects on or before
01.04.2019.
26. The projects, to be completed beyond March,
2019, are Haridwar I&D, Badrinath I&D with STP,
Joshimath I&D with STP, Haridwar 82 MLD STP, Muni-ki-Reti I&D with STP and Rishikesh I&D with STP. The
work executed as on 30.08.2018 qua these projects is
49.36% in I&D-I (Jagjeetpur), 62.52% in I&D-II (Sarai),
18% in Badrinath I&D, 21% in Joshimath I&D, 25.98%
in 68 MLD STP in Haridwar, 33.97% in 14 MLD STP
Haridwar, 27.40% in Muni-ki-Reti and 7% in Rishikesh.
Direction: We request all the Executing Agencies
including the NMCG, Union of India and other Agencies
to complete the work on or before 01.03.2020.
27. All the concerned District Magistrates shall be
personally responsible to comply with the directions
issued hereinabove and we also appoint the Secretary,
Drinking Water to the State of Uttarakhand as the Nodal
Officer to ensure that the directions, issued hereinabove,
are complied with obediently and punctually.
28. The writ petition stands disposed of in the
aforesaid terms.
29. We also place on record our appreciation for
the valuable assistance rendered by learned Advocates
appearing for the parties.
30. All pending applications stand disposed of
accordingly.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) (Rajiv Sharma, ACJ.)
 04.10.2018
NISHANT
